requirements.text: SM-2 is a pure, dependency-free module with an injected clock/calendar — no Date()/Calendar.current calls inside it.
SM-2 uses literal SuperMemo-2 arithmetic: EF' = EF + (0.1 − (5−q)×(0.08+(5−q)×0.02)), EF floored at 1.3; I(1)=1 day, I(2)=6 days, I(n)=round(I(n-1)×EF) for n>2.

Grade-to-quality mapping is fixed: Again=q2, Hard=q3, Good=q4, Easy=q5; a lapse is quality<3 only (Again), resetting repetition to 0 and interval to 1 day while still applying the EF decrease; Hard is a passing grade that advances normally.
SM-2 unit tests cover first review, lapse reset, EF floor, calendar-day boundary, a simulated DST transition, and a simulated mid-interval timezone change.
SM-2 includes at least one worked example cross-checked against a known external SM-2/Anki reference progression, with any divergence explained rather than treated as a bug.
Decks support create, edit, and archive.
Cards have front, back, and an optional note field, with fast keyboard-driven entry and editing.
Card deletion is supported and cascades to delete that card's ReviewLog history; resulting retroactive stat changes are expected behavior, not a bug.
Archived decks and their cards continue to count against Free-tier caps.
Review session shows due cards for a chosen deck or all decks, computed via calendar-day-at-query-time logic in the device's current timezone.
Review flow is front → tap to reveal → grade with Again/Hard/Good/Easy.
Each grade is persisted via an explicit synchronous save immediately after grading, before the next card advances — never relying on autosave.
Session summary (cards reviewed, again-rate, time spent) is shown only for a session that genuinely completed, never fabricated for an interrupted one.
Force-quitting mid-session, including a kill timed at/immediately after the save call, leaves graded cards off the due stack and ungraded cards still due on relaunch, with zero data loss.
Stats show a due-forecast bar chart for the next 30 days, per-deck and overall.
Stats show daily review-count history.
Stats show retention rate (% graded Good/Easy).
All stats screens handle empty and sparse data gracefully with honest, designed empty states — never a crash or misleading placeholder.
Demo-seeded decks/cards are excluded by default from aggregate/overall stats and streak calculations.
CSV export produces front, back, and optional note columns.
CSV import accepts front (required), back (required), and note (optional) columns, with a preview step before any data is committed.

CSV import preview enumerates a distinct, visible error reason for every malformed-row case: empty front/back, wrong column count, embedded commas/quotes, bad encoding/BOM, CRLF vs LF — never silently dropped.
CSV import flags duplicates as case-sensitive exact front+back matches, both within the imported file and against existing non-archived cards in the target deck, as their own distinct reason.
Export then re-import round-trips losslessly, including notes.
CSV import test fixtures include at least one real-world exported CSV in addition to hand-crafted edge cases.
One optional local daily reminder notification fires at a user-chosen time.
The notification body contains only a numeric due-card count — never card content, deck names, or subject matter.
No notification is scheduled or fires when the computed due count is 0.
The due count is recomputed at natural refresh points (foreground, background, post-session, day rollover) rather than fixed at scheduling time.
Notification permission denial is handled gracefully with no crash and a clear path to opt in later.
A Settings demo-data toggle seeds two decks with a realistic review history.
Demo decks/cards are visibly tagged everywhere they appear: deck list, review header, and stats breakdowns.
Demo data remains viewable individually when a user drills into that specific demo deck.
Disabling demo data removes it fully via one Settings action, with zero residue left in real stats or streaks.
All type, spacing, and color tokens live in a single Theme.swift referenced everywhere, with no literals scattered in views.
The app fully supports dark mode via semantic color roles, verified in both appearances on every screen.
Every reachable screen implements empty, loading, success, and error states as applicable to its workflow.
No UI affordance of any kind, including disabled/greyed-out controls, exists for out-of-scope infrastructure-dependent features.

A reviewer-visible gap/limitations register documents: cloud sync/accounts/marketplace non-goals with effort notes, the StoreKit purchase offline exception, notification due-count staleness, timezone-crossing due-status flips, and iCloud device-backup divergence across two devices.

Free tier includes the complete, fully correct core loop (SM-2, review, CSV import/export, stats) forever, capped only at 3 decks, 300 real (non-demo) cards, and 30 days of stats history plus the 30-day forecast.
Plus subscription removes the Free caps and adds per-deck local reminder-time customization.
A lapsed Plus subscription never deletes or hides any existing deck, card, or review history — it only blocks creating new content beyond the caps.
CSV import preview surfaces plan-cap-blocked rows as their own distinct, visible reason, separate from malformed-row and duplicate categories, never silently truncated.

The App Store purchase transaction is the sole exception to offline-forever; an airplane-mode test confirms the full app including an already-purchased entitlement works offline, with only the purchase sheet requiring network and failing gracefully.
No ads and no dark-pattern upgrade prompts; core correctness, scheduling accuracy, and review-flow speed are never paywalled.
Grading controls (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) are distinguishable without relying on color alone, via text and/or accessible VoiceOver labels.
Information architecture is a 3-tab shell: Study (deck list, due counts, review entry), Stats, and Settings & Tools.
The app runs the full core loop offline forever (airplane mode), with zero crashes or hangs from any implicit network call, except the documented StoreKit purchase exception.
No cloud sync, iCloud sync, accounts, push, or community/shared decks exist anywhere in the app.
No deck marketplace, no media/markdown/image/audio cards, and no sub-deck nesting exist anywhere in the app.
No ML-based scheduling beyond SM-2, no auto-tagging or smart difficulty inference, and no cross-deck merge/dedup logic exist anywhere in the app.
Hitting a Free-tier cap mid-review-session does not corrupt or block the in-progress review session.
Deck and card lists support text search and filter by active/archived status.
Stats charts support optional deeper interactions (focus/zoom) without degrading baseline clarity.
Property-based/fuzz tests exercise midnight and timezone-shift boundaries beyond the fixed required SM-2 test cases.
